catalog_quote: Kalau diperhatikan ucapan penutur bahasa Atinggola akan kedengaran tekanan-tekanan tertentu yang ternyata tidak menimbulkan perbedaan arti. Pola tekanan itu sebagai berikut. 1) Kata yang Bersuku Dua. Pada kata-kata yang bersuku dua, tekanan jatuh pada suku pertama dari belakang. Di sini tekanan dinyatakan dengan tanda ('). Contoh: /s'unge/ 'tanduk' /t'upa/ 'ketam' /s'opi/ 'sisir' /d'iu/ 'tidak'. 2) Kata yang Bersuku Tiga. Tekanannya jatuh pada suku kedua (suku tengah). Contoh: /has'ango/ 'insang' /ad'unda/ 'bagaimana' /bit'edi/ 'kambing' /moh'uwo/ 'banyak'. 3) Kata yang Bersuku Empat. Tekanannya jatuh pada suku ketiga. Contoh: /paRemp'ango/ 'pelepah daun kelapa' /moRimb'ungo/ 'pendek' /ninimp'oto/ 'bintang' /peab'uqo/ 'abu'. 4) Kata yang Bervokal Panjang. Bagi kata-kata yang bervokal panjang, tekanan jatuh pada suku kata yang bervokal panjang itu, baik yang bersuku dua maupun bersuku tiga dan seterusnya. Contoh-contoh di bawah ini akan diberikan berturut-turut dari yang bersuku dua. Contoh: /at'aa/ atau /wat'aa/ 'saya' /b'uuRu/ 'bor' /a'agu/ 'burung gagak' /b'eea/ 'ini' /R'aayaso/ 'bolak' /bib'iilo/ 'bambu penampung tuak' /p'oohoqo/ 'asap' /p'ooigua/ 'kamar mandi' /mom'oataqo/ 'makan banyak' /mod'aahagu/ 'kuning' /sos'aayugo/ 'sudip' /dum'oodupo/ 'pagi'

Pola tekanan itu sebagai berikut. 1) Kata yang Bersuku Dua: Pada kata-kata yang bersuku dua, tekanan jatuh pada suku pertama dari belakang. ... Contoh: /has'ango/ 'insang' ... 3) Kata yang Bersuku Empat: Tekanannya jatuh pada suku ketiga. new_statements.translation: If one listens to the speech of Atinggola speakers, certain stresses can be heard which turn out not to produce differences of meaning. The stress pattern is as follows. 1) Disyllabic words: in disyllabic words the stress falls on the first syllable from the back [sic; the marked examples /s'unge/ 'horn', /t'upa/ 'crab' carry it on the first = penultimate syllable]. 2) Trisyllabic words: the stress falls on the second (middle) syllable, e.g. /has'ango/ 'gills'. 3) Four-syllable words: the stress falls on the third syllable, e.g. /paRemp'ango/, /moRimb'ungo/ 'short'. 4) Words with a long vowel: for words containing a long vowel, the stress falls on the syllable with the long vowel, whether the word has two, three or more syllables, e.g. /R'aayaso/ 'bald', /mod'aahagu/ 'yellow'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: is held by the project (29 MB, 205 pp, PaperStream image-only scan, no text layer; PDF page = book page + 14), with the two extracted page images / and the scanned file. (our source list 'held' is empty but the directory and exist; I appended an independent-check note and saved the Glottolog languoid JSON there.) I read both page images by eye. Book p. 34 carries '2.2 Fonem Suprasegmental / 2.2.1 Tekanan' and the passage exactly as quoted: 'Kalau diperhatikan ucapan penutur bahasa Atinggola akan kedengaran tekanan-tekanan tertentu yang ternyata tidak menimbulkan perbedaan arti. Pola tekanan itu sebagai berikut. 1) Kata yang Bersuku Dua / Pada kata-kata yang bersuku dua, tekanan…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable (shown for 2-, 3- and 4-syllable words: first, second and third syllable respectively, with the stress mark placed before the penult vowel in every example); if the word contains a phonemically long vowel, that syllable carries the stress wherever it stands (examples include antepenultimate /mod'aahagu/, /dum'oodupo/ and final /at'aa/ 'I'). The wording 'suku pertama dari belakang' for disyllables is contradicted by the authors' own marked examples and by the parallel statements for 3- and 4-syllable words, all of which are penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: Long-vowel syllables attract the stress away from the penult (sec. 2.2.1 item 4, p. 34-35: /R'aayaso/, /p'oohoqo/, /mod'aahagu/, /sos'aayugo/, /dum'oodupo/ antepenult; /at'aa/ ~ /wat'aa/ final). No loanword or morphological exceptions discussed. Tingginehe et al. 1993:135 independently state that stress is not phonemic in Atinggola.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for isolated words (kata) classified by syllable count; examples are citation forms including some prefixed verbs (/mom'oataqo/, /mod'aahagu/), so the count appears to run over the whole affixed word. No phrase-level statement.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the Atinggola variety (bahasa Atinggola), fieldwork 1979/1980 in Kecamatan Atinggola (villages Kotajin, Monggupo, Pinontoyonga, Bintana, Imana, Buata, Gentuma; then Kabupaten Gorontalo, now Gorontalo Utara). Glottolog bola1252 'Bolango' / ISO bld covers both Atinggola and Bolango proper (south coast of Bolaang Mongondow Selatan); Sneddon & Usup 1986:409-410 treat them as closely related dialects (90% cognate) 'showing no differences in their phonological systems'. No first-hand stress statement for the Bolango dialect itself was found.

sources.note: Bab II Fonologi, 2.2 Fonem Suprasegmental, 2.2.1 Tekanan (pp. 34-35): stress audible but never distinguishes meaning; disyllables stressed on the first syllable (/s'unge/, /t'upa/), trisyllables on the second (/has'ango/), quadrisyllables on the third (/moRimb'ungo/) = penult throughout; words with a long vowel take stress on the long-vowel syllable (/R'aayaso/, /mod'aahagu/, /at'aa/).
